newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close higher on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close higher on speculative buying.

text.p: Strong buying by speculators and some foreign financial institutions (FIIs) pushed Delhi shares to a higher close on Tuesday, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 9.88 points higher at 749.16.
Marketmen said expectations that the government might introduce some measures to help the cement sector stoked fresh buying.
"Speculative buying wave was so strong that selling by profit-takers was also easily absorbed," said one broker.
Traders said buying was partly fuelled by hopes of a market-friendly budget.
Last week, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda had said the government would introduce some measures in the forthcoming budget to revive the capital markets and boost the economy.
"The market has turned volatile and likely to show two-way movements in coming sessions until the presentation of the financial budget," said Suresh Aggarwal of brokers Jai Mata Securities.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is expected to present the 1997/98 (April-March) budget on February 28.
Cement-maker ACC gained 54.25 rupees to 1,450 on heavy buying by speculators, brokers said.
State Bank of India shot up 9.45 rupees to 281.65 on heavy buying by FIIs, they said.
Larsen and Toubro rose 5.50 rupees to 247.50.
Reliance Industries quoted 3.45 rupees higher at 277.40.
